previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for fever and chills. He had a history of chronic pseudomonas-colonized skin ulcers and presented with new forearm lesions. Initial labs showed anemia, acute kidney injury, and hyperuricemia, all of which improved with IV fluids, rasburicase, and supportive care. He was started on empiric vancomycin and cefepime, but blood and wound cultures remained negative. Given clinical improvement and prior history, he was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and doxycycline. He developed mild fluid overload managed with diuresis and restart of torsemide. His GVHD was stable on ruxolitinib and sirolimus, and maggot therapy continued for wound care. He completed a course of IV antibiotics, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics with plans to resume prophylactic amoxicillin and IVIG post-discharge.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ man with history of AML s/p allo SCT 
complicated by extensive GVHD who is admitted with worsening 
shortness of breath, found to be volume overloaded.

# Acute on Chronic systolic heart failure
# Pulmonary GVHD
Mr ___ has chronic dyspnea related to restrictive physiology 
from
sclerosis along with pulmonary GVHD in addition to known 
systolic
heart failure. Examination by cardiology with bedside US was 
consistent with volume overload. He was actively diuresed with 
80 mg of IV Lasix, and his kidney function as well as his 
respiratory status improved. TTE did not reveal any acute 
changes in his heart function. He was transitioned to 40 mg of 
torsemide twice daily. He was net even on 40 mg of torsemide 
twice daily. He is maintained on telemetry throughout the stay. 
He was not initiated on lisinopril in the setting of an acute 
kidney injury, but this should be considered as an outpatient. 

# ___: 
Patient presented with acute kidney injury with a creatinine 
elevated to 1.5 by recent baseline of 1.0. Renal was consulted, 
and they additionally suggested his acute kidney injury was 
hemodynamically mediated in the setting of hyaline casts and 
elevated specific gravity, and sodium avid urine. His creatinine 
improved with diuresis, suggestive of cardiorenal physiology. 
His creatinine was 1.3 on discharge.

# Hyperuricemia 
Pt had hyperuricemia on presentation, which peaked at 11.4. This 
is thought to be secondary to his acute kidney injury. Renal was 
consulted and he recommended starting allopurinol. His uric acid 
was 9 on discharge. He was continued on his home rasburicase was 
not initiated as it is not thought to be necessary.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was performed without

MEDIASTINUM:  Mediastinal lymph nodes are not enlarged.

HEART:  The heart is not enlarged and there is moderate coronary arterial

VESSELS:  Vascular configuration is conventional.  Aortic caliber is normal.
